title: implement IAM-based peering acceptance and scheduled security-group rotation for private control plane
author: Maya Thakur
commits: 3a7d2e1 - add IAM role and assume-policy for cross-account peering acceptance
b24f9c7 - wire peering acceptance into provisioner and add acceptance script
d9cf3a2 - add SG templates and least-privilege baseline for control plane endpoints
f8114bd - scheduler to rotate SG rules with safe window and audit tags
e2a14f0 - helm chart: mount role ARN and enable installer flag
0d5b6ee - tests: integration coverage for peering acceptance and rollback path
c73b9a1 - docs: add rollout/rollback notes and operational runbook
description:
Motivation: Private control plane installs frequently require cross-account VPC peering (customer VPC <-> Redwood control plane) where manual acceptance is a recurring operational burden. Additionally, security teams requested an automated, auditable way to rotate and minimize security group (SG) blast radius for control-plane endpoints. This PR implements an IAM-based peering acceptance flow and a scheduled, auditable SG rotation mechanism to reduce manual steps and meet compliance guardrails.

What this changes (high level): Adds an optional IAM role that the customer's network account can grant the installer to perform 'AcceptVpcPeeringConnection' on behalf of the control plane. Introduces least-privilege SG templates for control-plane endpoints and a rotation scheduler that replaces ephemeral SG rules in a controlled maintenance window. Updates the Helm chart to accept the role ARN and toggles for the acceptance flow. Adds integration tests and runbook updates.

Implementation details: The new Terraform module modules/iam/peering-roles.tf creates a cross-account role with a tightly scoped assume-role policy and one action: ec2:AcceptVpcPeeringConnection (conditioned on the peering connection tag created by the installer). modules/network/peering.tf now tags peering resources with installer:peer-id to allow the role to target a single peering connection. scripts/accept-peering-via-role.sh is a small helper used by the installer control-plane agent when running in the customer's networking account via a delegated session.

Security group rotation: modules/sg/rotation/scheduler.tf provisions an optional Lambda+EventBridge (default disabled) or a CRON scheduler inside the on-prem operator that performs a blue->green swap of SG rules: it creates a new ephemeral SG with the same baseline, authorizes the new rules, atomically attaches the new SG set to the endpoints, and then removes the old rules. All changes are tagged with installer:rotation and rotation:id to make post-facto audits straightforward. The scheduler respects a configured maintenance window and a dry-run mode.

Helm and installer integration: helm/controlplane/templates/iam-role.yaml adds a ServiceAccount annotation that allows the control-plane installer pod to assume the cross-account role when run in a delegated deployment. values.yaml exposes installer.peering.accept_via_iam, installer.sg.rotation.enabled, windows and dry-run toggles. The installer includes a safe fallback: if role-based acceptance fails, it surfaces a clear actionable error and reverts to a manual acceptance instruction with a single command that operators can copy.

Testing and CI: Added tests/integration/test_peering_acceptance.py that spins up a short-lived responder account (local test harness) to simulate peering requests and validates that the acceptance is tightly scoped by tag and role. Terraform plan/apply continues to run in CI with a mock provider. End-to-end provisioning of a minimal control plane was exercised in a private integration job (e2e:controlplane-provision).

Rollout plan: Feature is behind two opt-in flags: installer.peering.accept_via_iam and installer.sg.rotation.enabled. Roll out to staging for a week, observe metrics (peering.accepted_via_role, sg.rotation.count, sg.rotation.failures) and audit logs. If errors exceed thresholds we will disable via a Helm patch and follow the rollback steps documented in installer/upgrade/rollback.md.

Backward compatibility and upgrade notes: Existing installs without the role are unaffected; the installer falls back to manual acceptance instructions. For customers who enable the IAM flow, we require a one-time customer action to create a role trust policy in their account (documented and automatable via a CloudFormation snippet in README.md). SG rotation defaults to disabled to avoid surprises.

Related work: ENG-2941 (reduce manual peering ops), ENG-3002 (sg hardening), SUP-1128 (support ticket with affected customer).

Files changed (summary): modules/iam/* (new role and policies), modules/network/peering.tf (tagging and outputs), modules/sg/* (templates + scheduler), helm/controlplane/* (values + templates), scripts/accept-peering-via-role.sh (helper), tests/integration/*, docs/README.md and installer/upgrade/rollback.md.

CI notes: First pipeline failed on tfsec warnings for overly-broad tags; tightened the policy and re-ran. All checks green on final run.

Requested reviewers: Security + Network to validate policy boundaries and customer-facing docs.

Merge: squash merge to keep the change tidy.
review_comments: Ethan Nguyen: Can we restrict the role further to only accept peering connections with tag installer:peer-id matching a pattern? (addressed in commit d9cf3a2)

Priya Kapoor: Need a clear safe-fallback plan if the role is deleted in the customer account mid-rotation. Suggested adding idempotent safety checks and a circuit-breaker (added in scheduler commit f8114bd).
Liam O'Connor: Please add the CloudFormation snippet to README to simplify customer onboarding (added).
Maya Thakur (author): replied - added tag-based condition, dry-run and circuit-breaker, and CFN snippet. Also included audit tags for rotation.id to correlate logs with rollouts.
release_notes: Optional IAM-based VPC peering acceptance (opt-in) and scheduled security group rotation for control-plane endpoints. Added operational runbook and CloudFormation snippet for customer onboarding.
